title: Transformers
summary: Explains how transformers work using mutual induction, turns ratio calculations, losses, laminated cores, power ratings, applications in power distribution and instrument, current and isolating transformers.

sections.heading: Transformer construction and principle
paragraphs: A transformer applies mutual induction: two separate coils of wire are wrapped onto a common laminated soft iron core. The field produced by each primary turn induces an emf in each secondary turn, so with equal turns the output voltage equals the input voltage (assuming no losses).

With more turns on the primary, the secondary voltage is lower, but the increased induction per secondary turn increases the available secondary current. The secondary voltage is stepped down but the current is stepped up.

sections.heading: Turns ratio relationships
paragraphs: The turns, voltages and currents are related by Np ÷ Ns = Vp ÷ Vs = Is ÷ Ip. Np and Ns are the turns on the primary and secondary windings, Vp and Vs the voltages, and Ip and Is the currents.
A transformer with 1000 primary turns and 100 secondary turns has a turns ratio of 10:1. The output voltage is 10 times lower (step-down) and the output current may be 10 times greater (step-up).
bullets: Worked example: 230 V supply, 1200 primary turns, 300 secondary turns: Vs = 230 × 300 ÷ 1200 = 57.5 V

sections.heading: Transformer losses
paragraphs: Losses occur in both the iron core and the inductive coil. The four main causes are hysteresis, eddy current, reactive and resistive losses.
bullets: Hysteresis: with an alternating field there is insufficient time for the molecular domains to fully align before polarity reverses, so the metal is never fully magnetised
Eddy currents: circulating electrons produce fields opposing the original field; they can reduce efficiency by as much as 80%
Reactive losses result from the reactance (XL = 2π f L) of the coils
Resistive losses result from the dc resistance of the copper windings
Reactive and resistive losses reduce the primary and secondary winding currents

sections.heading: Laminated core and power rating
paragraphs: A ferrous metal core (commonly iron or steel) keeps the flux near the windings by providing a low reluctance path compared with air, greatly increasing efficiency. A solid core would create large eddy currents, so a laminated core is used in power transformers.
Output power is measured in kVA or MVA, based on P = V×I. A rating of 20.7kVA at 230 volts gives a load current I = 20700VA ÷ 230V = 90 amperes.

sections.heading: Applications and power distribution
paragraphs: Transformers have three common functions: power distribution, voltage conversion and current measurement. They step voltages up and down at different points in the distribution network. High voltage is too dangerous at the point of use, so it is stepped down to a safer value.
bullets: UK voltages: generation 25kV; grid transmission 400kV or 275kV; distribution 132kV, 66kV, 33kV, 11kV, 400/230V
A dc transmission line between the UK and France removes normal ac losses (the ac supply is rectified to dc)

sections.heading: Instrument and isolating transformers
paragraphs: Instrument transformers have a secondary wound for low voltage, which simplifies insulation of the instrument and makes it safer. They isolate the instrument from the main circuit, allow remote reading, and standardise secondary voltage or current (usually 110V and 5A).
A current transformer (CT) must always be connected on the secondary side by a measuring instrument or a shorting link. If the secondary is left open circuit, a large voltage discharge will occur.
An isolating transformer has both sides electrically separate, giving a reduced shock risk.
bullets: Voltage transformer example: monitoring a 660V supply with a 110V voltmeter gives a turns ratio of 660 ÷ 110 = 6:1
CT example: 200A line current, 5A full scale, 2 primary turns gives 2 ÷ Ns = 5 ÷ 200, so Ns = 80 turns

flashcards.front: What is the practical application of mutual induction?
flashcards.back: The transformer, with two coils wound on a common laminated soft iron core.

flashcards.front: What happens to voltage and current in a step-down transformer?
flashcards.back: The secondary voltage is stepped down and the current is stepped up.

flashcards.front: What is the turns ratio relationship?
flashcards.back: Np ÷ Ns = Vp ÷ Vs = Is ÷ Ip.

flashcards.front: What turns ratio does 1000 primary and 100 secondary turns give?
flashcards.back: 10:1, so the output voltage is 10 times lower and output current may be 10 times greater.

flashcards.front: Name the four main transformer losses.
flashcards.back: Hysteresis, eddy current, reactive and resistive losses.
The dc resistance in the copper coil windings.

flashcards.front: Why is a laminated core used?
flashcards.back: A solid metal core would create large eddy currents.

flashcards.front: Why is the core a low reluctance path?
flashcards.back: A ferrous core maintains flux near the windings, compared with the surrounding air path, greatly increasing efficiency.

flashcards.front: In what units is transformer output power rated?
What are the three common functions of transformers?
flashcards.back: Power distribution, voltage conversion and current measurement.

flashcards.front: What must you ensure with a current transformer's secondary?
flashcards.back: It is always connected to a measuring instrument or shorting link; open circuit causes a large voltage discharge.

flashcards.front: What does an isolating transformer provide?
flashcards.back: Electrical separation of both sides and a reduced shock risk.

quiz.q: A 230 V supply feeds 1200 primary turns. What emf is induced in a 300-turn secondary (Np ÷ Ns = Vp ÷ Vs)?
A transformer has 1000 primary and 100 secondary turns. What is the effect?
options: Voltage and current both rise 10 times
Voltage is 10 times lower and current may be 10 times greater
Voltage 10 times greater, current 10 times lower
quiz.why: A 10:1 ratio steps voltage down and current up.

quiz.q: Which is NOT one of the four main causes of transformer loss?
quiz.why: The four are hysteresis, eddy current, reactive and resistive losses.

quiz.q: What is the load current for a 20.7kVA transformer at 230 volts?
Why is a laminated core used in power transformers?
quiz.why: A solid core would create large eddy currents, so laminations are used.

quiz.q: What turns ratio is needed to monitor a 660V supply with a 110V voltmeter?
An ammeter with 5A full scale measures 200A using 2 primary turns. How many secondary turns?
What must never be done with a current transformer's secondary?
options: Connect it to a shorting link
Connect it to a measuring instrument
quiz.why: An open circuit secondary causes a large voltage discharge.

quiz.q: Which is a standard instrument transformer secondary value?
quiz.why: Secondary voltage or current is usually standardised at 110V and 5A.

quiz.q: What does an isolating transformer provide?
options: Electrically separate sides and reduced shock risk
quiz.why: Both sides are electrically separate, giving reduced shock risk.
